title: Evented Adapter API: SDK backpressure hooks and tool-call replay examples (TS/Py/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: As we expand the SDKs to support progressive streaming, tool/function calls, and structured outputs across TypeScript, Python, and Go, we need a clear adapter pattern that surfaces backpressure and replay semantics to client apps. Current examples show steady-state streaming and structured tool outputs, but lack primitives for: (1) signaling consumer-side backpressure hooks so host apps can apply adaptive batching or drop strategies; (2) canonical event framing that enables deterministic tool-call replay for idempotent side effects; and (3) consistent, minimal interfaces across TS/Py/Go with pragmatic examples that teams can copy into production. This ticket defines an "Evented Adapter API" sketch, implementation tasks for each SDK, and a small example app per language that demonstrates: (a) streaming tokens + tool-call events interleaved; (b) consumer backpressure signaling and pause/resume semantics; (c) tool-call replay with session tokens and idempotency keys; (d) conversion to typed structured outputs (JSON schemas) with error handling.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by SDK leads describing event envelope v2 and backpressure semantics
TS/Py/Go SDKs expose a minimal EventedAdapter interface with pause/resume and onEvent callbacks

Language examples (one per TS/Py/Go) demonstrate: streaming generation + tool invocation, a backpressure scenario where consumer asks for pause for 150ms and then resumes, and successful replay of a tool-call using stored session metadata
Unit tests for backpressure hook and replay logic with >=90% coverage for the adapter layer
Integration test showing structured output mapping to a JSON schema and fallback to validation error event
Documentation snippets (README + examples) merged into the SDK repo and referenced from the Console docs
implementation_notes: Event envelope v2: unify fields {type, seq, session_id, idempotency_key, payload} where payload is string or JSON stringified structured output

Backpressure hooks: provide adapter.pause() / adapter.resume() and an optional onBackpressure(callback) for consumer-driven signals; SDK should buffer up to N events then apply overflow policy (drop/slow-path/durable-queue)

Tool-call replay: when tool event emitted, SDK persists minimal replay record (session_id, seq, tool_name, args_hash, idempotency_key) to app-provided storage hook; replay API must accept replacement tool handler and guarantee at-most-once semantics using idempotency_key
Typed outputs: allow user to register schema validators per route; on structured output mismatch emit a validation_error event with original payload and suggested coercions
API ergonomics: keep surface small — EventedAdapter + StreamSession object; avoid language-specific heavy generics to keep parity across SDKs
Performance: ensure pause/resume has <10ms typical propagation in TS runtime and <30ms in Py/Go in our benchmarks; measure impact on throughput and tail-latency in existing test harness
testing_plan: Unit tests: simulate rapid event flood and assert adapter.pause() causes SDK to stop invoking onEvent for the given session; validate buffer overflow policy behaviors
Replay tests: inject a tool-call event, simulate process crash, restore SDK with recorded replay store and assert tool handler not double-invoked when idempotency_key present
Cross-language interoperability test: TS producer emits event stream, Go consumer uses EventedAdapter to resume/replay; asserts session metadata preserved
Schema validation test: send structured output that fails validator and assert validation_error event emitted and consumer can accept or request coercion
Performance tests: run workload with realistic token distribution to measure pause/resume latency, throughput drop, and memory footprint under high concurrency
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout in SDK packages behind `eventedAdapter` opt-in flag
Publish beta examples in SDK repos with examples/adapter-demo in each language
Invite 2 internal teams (Console traces team, Dedicated autoscaler) to try beta and collect feedback for 2 weeks
After stabilization, enable flag by default in next minor SDK release and update public docs + migration guide
